item: A finished rollup is asked the serve's first query before it is served (R157), and queries the engine refuses later are counted
summary: Builds that fit the 1,004 MB limit left no room for the queries that use them: the 30-day top-terms query ran out of memory on the resident rollup at 16 M mentions and every query did at 20 M, and the serve fell back to the live scan without saying so. columnar.serve_canary now runs that query once after a build, on the connection nobody else holds, with a 60 s cap and a polled peak. The engine's own memory error makes the build a duckdb-limit stop at stage serve-check (query, peak_mib, resident_mib; nothing is swapped in; kept and released by the rules a duckdb-limit stop already has); any other error is inconclusive and never blocks the rollup. The canary and the serve run one query text. rollup_serve.status() gains serve_fallbacks (served queries that fell back, by query and error class). Measured: see the OPEN_QUEUE note. No constants change.
